title: Jewish History: Am Yisrael and Eretz Yisrael

connections.label: Return to Zion and Second Temple

events.label: Anno Mundi 1: Hebrew calendar epoch
events.blurb: Rabbinic reckoning places creation in 3761 BCE, the start of the Hebrew year count; this is a religious chronology, not a historical date.

events.label: Covenant with Avraham (tradition)
events.blurb: Genesis presents God's covenant with Avraham and the promise of the land as the founding of the Jewish people; the date is traditional and has no outside attestation.

events.label: Exodus and Matan Torah at Sinai
events.blurb: The exodus from Egypt and the giving of the Torah are the central memory of Jewish identity; historicity is debated, and scholars who accept a core event usually place it in the 13th century BCE.

events.label: Merneptah Stele names Israel
events.blurb: An Egyptian victory inscription lists a people called Israel in Canaan, the oldest known reference to Israel outside the Bible.

events.label: Kingdom of David and Shlomo
events.blurb: Tradition holds that David made Jerusalem his capital and Shlomo (Solomon) built the Temple; archaeologists debate how large this united kingdom was.

events.label: First Temple built
events.blurb: Solomon's Temple on Mount Moriah becomes the center of Israelite worship (traditional date).

events.label: Tel Dan Stele: House of David
events.blurb: An Aramaic victory inscription mentions the 'House of David', the earliest outside reference to David's dynasty (9th century BCE, date approximate).

events.label: Assyria exiles the Ten Tribes
events.blurb: Samaria falls and the northern kingdom of Israel is deported, remembered as the loss of the Ten Tribes.

events.label: Hezekiah withstands Sennacherib
events.blurb: Jerusalem survives the Assyrian siege; Hezekiah's water tunnel still runs under the City of David.

events.label: Reform of King Josiah
events.blurb: Josiah centralizes worship in Jerusalem after a scroll of the Torah is found; many scholars connect it with Deuteronomy.

events.label: Destruction of the First Temple
events.blurb: Babylon burns Jerusalem and the Temple (586 or 587 BCE), mourned every year on Tisha B'Av.

events.label: Babylonian Exile
events.blurb: Exiled Judeans vow in Psalm 137 never to forget Jerusalem, and the community in Babylon lays foundations of diaspora Judaism.

events.label: Cyrus decree: return to Zion
events.blurb: Persian king Cyrus permits exiles to return and rebuild the Temple, the first Shivat Zion.

events.label: Second Temple completed
events.blurb: The rebuilt Temple is dedicated in Jerusalem under Persian rule.

events.label: Ezra and Nehemiah
events.blurb: Ezra's public reading of the Torah and Nehemiah's rebuilding of the walls renew Judean communal life (dates debated).

events.label: Maccabean revolt
events.blurb: Judeans led by the Hasmonean family revolt against the Seleucid ban on Torah observance.

events.label: Temple rededicated: Chanukah
events.blurb: The Maccabees purify and rededicate the Temple, the origin of Chanukah.

events.label: Hasmonean kingdom
events.blurb: The last independent Jewish state before 1948.

events.label: Pompey takes Jerusalem
events.blurb: Rome intervenes in a Hasmonean civil war and Judea becomes a Roman client.

events.label: Herod expands the Temple Mount
events.blurb: Herod's rebuilding produces the retaining wall now called the Kotel, the Western Wall.

events.label: Great Revolt against Rome
events.blurb: Judea rises against Roman rule; the war ends with the fall of Jerusalem and Masada.

events.label: Destruction of the Second Temple
events.blurb: Titus destroys Jerusalem and the Temple on Tisha B'Av, beginning nearly two millennia of exile from sovereignty.

events.label: Academy at Yavne
events.blurb: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai's academy reorients Judaism around Torah study, prayer, and rabbinic law.

events.label: Fall of Masada
events.blurb: The last rebel fortress falls (73 or 74 CE); Josephus describes the defenders choosing death over capture.

events.label: Bar Kokhba revolt
events.blurb: Rome crushes the last great revolt, bars Jews from Jerusalem, and renames Judea as Syria Palaestina.

events.label: Mishnah compiled
events.blurb: Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi edits the Oral Torah in the Galilee (c. 200 CE).

events.label: Jerusalem Talmud
events.blurb: Galilean academies complete the Talmud of the Land of Israel (c. 400 CE).

events.label: Babylonian Talmud completed
events.blurb: The Talmud Bavli, redacted in Babylonia (c. 500 CE, date approximate), becomes the core text of rabbinic law.

events.label: Aleppo Codex, Tiberias
events.blurb: Masoretes in Tiberias fix the vowels and text of the Hebrew Bible (c. 930 CE).

events.label: Golden Age of Sepharad
events.blurb: Under Muslim rule in Spain, Jewish poetry, philosophy and science flourish, from Ibn Gabirol to Yehuda HaLevi (dates approximate).

events.label: Rashi
events.blurb: Rashi of Troyes writes the standard commentaries on the Torah and Talmud.

events.label: Rhineland massacres of 1096
events.blurb: First Crusade armies destroy the Jewish communities of Speyer, Worms and Mainz, remembered as Gezerot Tatnu.

events.label: Rambam (Maimonides)
events.blurb: Maimonides writes the Mishneh Torah and the Guide for the Perplexed.

events.label: Expulsion from England
events.blurb: Edward I expels the Jews of England, the first of the major medieval expulsions.

events.label: Expulsion from Spain
events.blurb: Ferdinand and Isabella expel Spain's Jews; the Sephardi diaspora spreads to the Ottoman Empire, North Africa and the Netherlands.

events.label: Safed: Karo and the Ari
events.blurb: Joseph Karo's Shulchan Aruch (1565) and Isaac Luria's kabbalah make Safed a center of Jewish learning in Eretz Yisrael.

events.label: Gezerot Tach VeTat
events.blurb: Khmelnytsky's Cossack uprising kills tens of thousands of Jews in Ukraine (1648-49; totals debated).

events.label: Sabbatai Zevi movement
events.blurb: A mass messianic movement collapses when Sabbatai Zevi converts to Islam in 1666.

events.label: Baal Shem Tov and Hasidism
events.blurb: Hasidism emphasizes joy and devotion and spreads across Eastern Europe (founding date approximate).

events.label: Haskalah: Mendelssohn
events.blurb: Moses Mendelssohn's Jerusalem argues for Jewish civic participation, a landmark of the Jewish Enlightenment.

events.label: Emancipation in France
events.blurb: Revolutionary France grants Jews full citizenship, the first European state to do so.

events.label: Pogroms of 1881
events.blurb: Anti-Jewish riots across the Russian Empire, the Sufot BaNegev, push Jews toward emigration and Zionism.

events.label: First Aliyah
events.blurb: Bilu and Hovevei Zion pioneers found moshavot such as Rishon LeZion and Zichron Yaakov.

events.label: Herzl: Der Judenstaat
events.blurb: Theodor Herzl argues that only a Jewish state can solve the Jewish question.

events.label: First Zionist Congress, Basel
events.blurb: The Basel Program calls for a publicly secured home for the Jewish people in Eretz Yisrael.

events.label: Second Aliyah
events.blurb: Socialist pioneers, including Ben-Gurion, build Hebrew labor and the first kvutzot.

events.label: Tel Aviv founded
events.blurb: Families from Jaffa found Ahuzat Bayit, which becomes Tel Aviv, the first modern Hebrew city.

events.label: Degania, first kvutza
events.blurb: A collective farm on the Sea of Galilee, the forerunner of the kibbutz movement.

events.label: Balfour Declaration
events.blurb: Britain declares support for a national home for the Jewish people in Palestine.

events.label: League of Nations Mandate
events.blurb: The Mandate charges Britain with implementing the Balfour Declaration and recognizes the Jewish historical connection to the land.

events.label: Tarpat riots and Hebron massacre
events.blurb: Arab rioters kill 133 Jews, including about 67 in Hebron, ending the city's ancient Jewish community until after 1967.

events.label: The Events of 1936-1939
events.blurb: The Yishuv defends its settlements during the Arab uprising, and the Peel Commission proposes the first partition (1937).

events.label: 1939 White Paper
events.blurb: Britain caps Jewish immigration at 75,000 over five years as Europe's Jews try to escape the Nazis.

events.label: The Shoah
events.blurb: Nazi Germany and its collaborators murder about six million Jews, a third of the Jewish people.

events.label: UN Partition Plan accepted
events.blurb: The Jewish Agency accepts UN Resolution 181; Arab leaders reject it and fighting begins.

events.label: Declaration of Independence
events.blurb: David Ben-Gurion proclaims the State of Israel in Tel Aviv on 5 Iyar 5708.

events.label: War of Independence
events.blurb: Five Arab armies invade the new state; about 6,000 Israelis are killed, roughly 1% of the Jewish population.

events.label: Exodus of Jews from Arab lands
events.blurb: Jewish communities in the Arab world are expelled or pressured out, a total commonly given as about 850,000; most resettle in Israel.

events.label: Law of Return
events.blurb: Every Jew gains the right to immigrate to Israel and become a citizen.

events.label: Eichmann trial
events.blurb: Israel tries a central organizer of the Shoah, bringing survivor testimony to the world.

events.label: Six-Day War: Jerusalem reunited
events.blurb: Facing Arab mobilization, Israel takes Sinai, Gaza, Judea and Samaria, and the Golan, and Jews return to the Old City and the Kotel.

events.label: Munich massacre
events.blurb: Black September terrorists murder eleven Israeli Olympic athletes and coaches.

events.label: Yom Kippur War
events.blurb: Egypt and Syria launch a surprise attack on the holiest day of the year; Israel recovers at a cost of about 2,700 dead.

events.label: Operation Entebbe
events.blurb: Commandos rescue hostages from a hijacked airliner in Uganda.

events.label: Peace treaty with Egypt
events.blurb: Begin and Sadat sign the first peace between Israel and an Arab state, returning Sinai.

events.label: Operation Peace for Galilee
events.blurb: Israel invades Lebanon to expel the PLO; the Kahan Commission later finds Defense Minister Sharon indirectly responsible for Sabra and Shatila.

events.label: Operations Moses and Solomon
events.blurb: Airlifts bring most of Ethiopian Jewry (Beta Israel) to Israel.

events.label: First Intifada
events.blurb: A Palestinian uprising in Judea, Samaria and Gaza challenges Israeli rule.

events.label: Aliyah from the former USSR
events.blurb: About one million immigrants arrive after the Soviet collapse, reshaping Israeli society.

events.label: Oslo Accords
events.blurb: Rabin and Arafat sign mutual recognition and an interim self-rule framework.

events.label: Peace treaty with Jordan
events.blurb: Israel and Jordan sign a full peace treaty.

events.label: Rabin assassinated
events.blurb: A Jewish extremist opposed to Oslo murders Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin.

events.label: Second Intifada
events.blurb: Suicide bombings and attacks kill about 1,000 Israelis; Israel builds the security barrier.

events.label: Disengagement from Gaza
events.blurb: Israel removes all settlements and soldiers from the Gaza Strip.

events.label: Second Lebanon War
events.blurb: A month-long war with Hezbollah follows a cross-border raid.

events.label: Abraham Accords
events.blurb: Israel normalizes relations with the UAE, Bahrain, Morocco and Sudan.

events.label: Judicial overhaul protests
events.blurb: Mass protests oppose the government's plan to curb the Supreme Court.

events.label: October 7: Simchat Torah massacre
events.blurb: Hamas-led terrorists kill about 1,200 people, mostly civilians, and take 251 hostages, the deadliest day for Jews since the Shoah.

events.label: Swords of Iron War
events.blurb: Israel fights to destroy Hamas and bring the hostages home; Israel rejects the genocide charge brought by South Africa at the ICJ.

events.label: Twelve-Day War with Iran
events.blurb: Operation Rising Lion strikes Iran's nuclear and missile programs; Iran fires missiles at Israeli cities.

events.label: Last living hostages come home
events.blurb: Hamas releases the 20 remaining living hostages under the October 2025 ceasefire.

events.label: 26th Knesset election
events.blurb: The first Knesset election held on its scheduled date since 1988; results are not included here.
